entries.title: Mulberry may reshape gut bacteria and influence metabolism
entries.summary: Mulberry compounds may reshape the gut microbiome in ways that support intestinal health and metabolism, with some combinations showing especially strong effects in animal studies. entries.title: Bats may have first evolved in Europe 65 million years ago

entries.title: A broken rib from the world’s largest T. rex hid a 66-million-year-old secret

entries.summary: A newly identified 240-million-year-old animal from Tanzania is forcing scientists to rethink the early dinosaur timeline. entries.summary: A 120-million-year-old fossil forgotten in a museum for nearly a century has revealed a terrifying new dinosaur that may have been more dangerous to humans than a T. rex. entries.title: Cornell scientists identify rare human genetic disorder in two unusually long-legged cats

entries.summary: A massive prehistoric snake discovered in India may have rivaled the largest snake ever known. entries.title: Scientists finally see DNA “zip” itself together for the first time

entries.title: This 245-million-year-old fossil still has its stomach and intestines
entries.summary: A 245-million-year-old marine reptile fossil preserves an astonishing amount of detail, including its stomach, liver, and intestines. The discovery reveals that Austronaga minuta was highly adapted for swimming even though its digestive system remained surprisingly simple.

entries.title: Scientists discover a bizarre Jurassic “squid” unlike anything ever seen
entries.summary: Scientists have identified the “fattest” belemnite ever discovered, a bizarre, barrel-shaped squid relative that lived in Wyoming’s ancient seas 160 million years ago. entries.title: UV light reveals possible camouflage on a 125-million-year-old crocodile

entries.title: 210-million-year-old dinosaur discovery reveals a lost world in Africa

entries.title: This tiny jurassic predator helped pave the way for the human brain
entries.summary: A 165-million-year-old fossil has revealed an extraordinary Jurassic predator that may help explain how mammals developed one of their most important evolutionary advantages. entries.title: DNA recording system reveals how a single cell becomes a body

entries.title: A new way to fight gum disease without wiping out good bacteria
entries.summary: Scientists discovered that disrupting the chemical messages bacteria use to communicate can push dental plaque toward a healthier microbial balance. The approach could lead to new treatments for gum disease that control harmful bacteria without destroying beneficial species.

entries.title: Humans may not be as hardwired for violence as we thought
entries.summary: A study comparing 100 primate species, including humans, suggests that everyday aggression and lethal violence did not evolve as part of the same simple behavioral spectrum. entries.title: Animals may have evolved 200 million years earlier than we thought

entries.title: Scientists find two tiny new snails with shells that close like doors
entries.summary: Scientists discovered two tiny new snail species in Montenegro, showing that even Europe still holds animals unknown to science. One lives in the threatened Komarnica Canyon, where a proposed hydropower reservoir could destroy habitat before its full biodiversity is understood.

entries.title: Scientists discover a mysterious new frog hiding in the Amazon

entries.title: “Crawzilla” was huge. Then scientists found an even bigger crayfish
entries.summary: A nationwide search for giant crayfish uncovered a record-breaking Tennessee specimen and a surprising mystery about how big these freshwater creatures can grow. Scientists found that North American crayfish seem to hit a biological size limit, possibly because of their muscles or protective shells.

entries.title: A fungus is threatening the world’s food supply. Scientists just found a new defense

entries.title: Scientists accidentally discover a genetic code that breaks the rules of life

entries.title: This “golden tree” coral was too strange for any known family
entries.summary: A brilliant yellow coral discovered off Costa Rica proved so unusual that scientists had to create an entirely new family to classify it. entries.title: This giant stick insect fooled scientists for decades

entries.title: New soil test could reveal how soil microbes help feed plants
entries.summary: Scientists have streamlined a method for measuring DNA-bound phosphorus in soil, making it cheaper and easier while preserving its accuracy. The technique could reveal how soil microbes help recycle phosphorus and ultimately support more sustainable fertilizer and nutrient management.

entries.title: 1.7-billion-year-old fossils reveal a crucial clue to the rise of complex life
entries.summary: Scientists studying ancient Australian rocks uncovered more than 12,000 fossils from some of the oldest known eukaryotes on Earth. entries.title: Scientists discover a hidden “ID card” in cat urine
entries.summary: Cats may identify one another through a surprisingly durable chemical “calling card” made from 13 unusual fatty acids in their urine. The compounds appear linked to mysterious fat droplets in the kidneys and may represent a scent-recognition system shared across the cat family.

entries.title: NASA-backed scientists turn plastic waste into edible cookies
entries.summary: Scientists have engineered yeast to turn PET plastic and agricultural waste into ingredients for protein-rich, 3D-printed cookies called µBites. entries.title: Scientists discover why a 100-year-old mushroom disease won't go away

entries.title: The “glue” holding your cells together has a surprising second job

entries.title: Scientists say house cats could help unlock better cancer treatments for humans
entries.summary: Scientists have mapped the genetics of cat cancer on an unprecedented scale and found surprising similarities with tumors in humans. The findings could help bring precision cancer treatments to cats while also revealing new clues about how human cancers develop and respond to drugs.

entries.title: This tiny organism can shrink to one quarter its size in milliseconds
entries.summary: A single-celled organism can shrink to one-quarter of its length in milliseconds using a remarkable calcium-powered protein “fishnet.” Scientists hope its unusual machinery could inspire artificial muscles capable of moving far faster than today’s designs.

entries.title: Archaeologists discover 1,200-year-old mummified hairless dog in Peru
entries.summary: Archaeologists have discovered 1,200-year-old remains of Peru’s famous hairless dogs at an ancient Wari Empire burial site, including remarkably preserved mummies and puppies buried alongside humans. entries.title: Leucine does more than build muscle. It powers up your cells
entries.summary: The essential amino acid leucine can boost cellular energy production by protecting key proteins on mitochondria from being destroyed. The discovery reveals a new connection between nutrition and metabolism that could eventually lead to new approaches for metabolic disorders and cancer.

entries.title: The secret to longer life may be hidden in bat DNA
entries.summary: Long-lived bats appear to combine powerful immune defenses with unusual strategies for eliminating damaged cells, potentially helping them avoid cancer and disease for decades.
